item.title: Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf pull off miracle with record 89-run partnership for last wicket as Pakistan stun England in Lahore
item.description: The game looked set for England when Haris Rauf walked out to bat at number 11 with Pakistan at 154 for 9 in their chase of 242, still needing 88 runs to win. It looked like it was all over, and England certainly thought so. But Shadab Khan, who came in at number eight, did the unthinkable, stitching together an unbeaten 89-run partnership for the last wicket with Rauf to take Pakistan home in Lahore on Sunday. in the fourth ODI of the tri-series, which also features Sri Lanka. Shadab chipped away at the target, finding a boundary in almost every over while managing to keep the strike with himself most of the time. Rauf played his part too, defending when needed and ducking and weaving as England threw everything at him. He hung in there to finish unbeaten on seven, while Shadab dictated terms at the other end. Rauf eventually hit the winning runs and raced away with his arms raised. The unbeaten 89-run stand between Shadab and Rauf is now the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI chase. The previous record was an unbeaten 64-run partnership between Deryck Murray and Andy Roberts against Pakistan at the 1975 World Cup. Shadab scored his maiden ODI century, making 113 off 96 balls in a match-winning effort that turned the game on its head as England let victory slip away. The win took Pakistan into the tri-series final. — PakistanCrnrj (@PakistanCrnrj) England had made a strong start while defending their target, with their bowlers working together to prevent Pakistan from building partnerships. Pakistan lost their top three batters — Fakhar Zaman (10 off 18), Saim Ayub (6 off 12) and Babar Azam (10 off 12) — inside the powerplay. England continued to take wickets and reduced the hosts to 154 for 9, but could not get the final breakthrough as Shadab and Rauf guided Pakistan to a memorable win in Lahore. Earlier, Pakistan captain and fast bowler Shaheen Shah Afridi took four wickets to restrict England to 241, despite a fighting century from Ben Duckett. England, who needed a win to stay in contention for the tri-series after losing their first two matches, struggled to recover after slipping to 19 for 3 on a batting-friendly pitch. Duckett scored 105 off 111 balls, while Sam Curran made 42 during a 93-run stand for the fifth wicket. Gus Atkinson added an unbeaten 36 towards the end of the innings. Shaheen finished with figures of 4 for 46, while ODI debutant Razaullah took 2 for 38 as England were bowled out in 46.4 overs.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli Dominates United States Grand Prix to Claim Ninth Win of the Season
item.description: Photo by: JEROME MIRON Mercedes Star Moves Closer to Historic Formula 1 Championship Kimi Antonelli continued his incredible 2026 Formula 1 season Sunday, winning the United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. The Mercedes driver delivered a dominant performance to claim his ninth victory of the season and move one step closer to securing his first world championship. Antonelli crossed the finish line more than 13 seconds ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, while Red Bull’s Max Verstappen completed the podium in third place. The victory further established the 20-year-old Italian as the driver to beat as the season approaches its conclusion. Starting from pole position, Antonelli made an excellent opening lap and quickly established control of the race. His strong start allowed him to build an early advantage while Verstappen and Leclerc battled behind him. Antonelli Makes the Right Strategy Work While several competitors faced challenges managing their tires, Antonelli and Mercedes executed an effective one stop strategy that helped him maintain his advantage throughout the race. Antonelli delivered an impressive stint on medium tires before switching to the hard compound. He managed his tires effectively and maintained a strong pace, allowing him to control the race even as the pressure increased behind him. Leclerc eventually moved ahead of Verstappen to secure second place, but neither driver could seriously threaten Antonelli’s lead. The Mercedes star remained composed through the closing laps and brought home another major victory. Lewis Hamilton finished fourth for Ferrari, while McLaren’s Lando Norris settled for fifth. Oscar Piastri finished seventh, and Mercedes teammate George Russell crossed the line in eighth after receiving a five second penalty. Championship Dreams Getting Closer Although Antonelli won the race, he did not clinch the championship in Austin. Russell’s eighth place finish and Hamilton’s fourth place result kept the title mathematically undecided. However, Antonelli now holds a commanding championship advantage and needs only a ninth place finish at next weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix to guarantee the title, regardless of his rivals’ results. If he secures the championship, Antonelli would become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, surpassing Sebastian Vettel’s record. With five races remaining, Antonelli has put himself in an excellent position to complete a remarkable season. His latest victory demonstrates his consistency, composure and ability to deliver under pressure. The young Italian will now head to Mexico with history within reach. After another commanding performance in Austin, Antonelli is closer than ever to becoming Formula 1’s next world champion.

item.description: Kimi Antonelli has won nine of the 18 races so far this season [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli just missed out on clinching his first world title in a dominant victory in the United States Grand Prix. The 20-year-old Italian leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 123 points after coming home ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc. Antonelli will be crowned champion in Mexico City next weekend as long he does not lose more than 23 points to Russell and 24 to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. That means a ninth place would be enough to become champion even if Russell wins the race, and a 10th would be enough if Hamilton is victorious. If Russell or Hamilton do not win, Antonelli will be champion next Sunday no matter where he finishes. Antonelli stamped his authority on this race in the same way as he has on the season, and was out of touch even by the first corner as his rivals all battled behind him. The key stories of the race were: Antonelli's sublime victory, his first since the Spanish Grand Prix last month A race-long squabble between Leclerc and Verstappen for second place Little else, frankly Antonelli took control of the race from the very beginning, an excellent start combined with a gripping scrap through the first lap between Verstappen and Leclerc leaving him more than two seconds clear by the end of the first lap. The entertainment was provided by Leclerc and Verstappen, initially wheel to wheel and then at a distance as divergent strategies played out. Leclerc, who started fourth, jumped up to third place behind Verstappen on the exit of the first corner, and then bravely sat it out around the outside of the Red Bull through the high speed Turn Three at the start of the Esses and then dived down the inside into Turn Four. Verstappen, though, was not finished, and he closed in on Leclerc down the back straight and they fought hard through the switchback series of corners through the stadium section before the Dutchman claimed second place with a dive down the inside of Turn 15. Verstappen led Leclerc to his first stop on lap 13, Ferrari waiting two laps longer before the Monegasque made his own first stop. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Alpine's Pierre Gasly claimed the final points positions in ninth and 10th. item.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd owners' problems far bigger
item.description: There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the Manchester United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss. But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for the United boss. However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise. On Friday, as he looked back on that 4-1 loss to Como and ahead to Bournemouth, Carrick said: "We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday." Sadly, they weren't. Carrick could not answer if he will still be in charge for next Saturday's trip to Chelsea. He does not know. "The responsibility is mine," he said. "What else can I say really right now? I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club." If that wasn't enough, a ticket touting investigation launched in the summer led to condemnation from all United's major fan groups. The club argued they were trying to catch touts, while fans felt it was an attempt to drive regular match-goers out in favour of more corporate sales. The club conducted a survey which they said showed the majority of respondents were in favour of a new ground. The stadium is likely to cost in excess of £2bn and United spent £63.5m on land for it earlier this year. Some supporters simply don't believe those figures. item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning celebrates with his mother Ellen Heidingsfelder Manning after beating the Mississippi Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) No one ever questioned his toughness. Arch Manning doesn't mind getting hit and his alpha dog nature has earned the respect of his teammates and coaches. The man took a beating Saturday night against No. 7 Ole Miss and never flinched. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks for a receiver in the first quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) And most important, he was leading the Texas Longhorns to a much-needed win. "He's a fighter," Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said. "I like the edgy, kind of borderline, arrogant, full of swagger Arch and I feel like that's when he's at his best. Our team feeds off the energy, too." UP NEXT NO. 11 TEXAS VS. MISSISSIPPI STATE When/where: 6:30 p.m. Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium. TV/radio: ESPN; 1300 AM, 98.1 FM, 105.3 FM (Spanish). MORE HORNS : Best photos from Texas-Ole Miss The biggest issue surrounding the face of the Texas program is that Manning has become an all-or-nothing quarterback, a recipe that's not conducive to ultimate success. He earned kudos for his gutty display in Saturday's 34-27 nail biter , but some of his decisions were troubling. While we must credit him for the three touchdowns he produced - one passing and two rushing scores - we must also discuss the lost fumble and the two interceptions that pushed his season total to seven. Six giveaways in his last three games are nowhere near the type of clean football Manning played down the stretch last season. A real cleanup is needed in that area. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning and running back Raleek Brown celebrate after beating Mississippi at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) A great start for Arch Manning, but not so great later Let's give Manning some flowers first. He played wonderfully in the first half. He delivered a perfect aerial to Cam Coleman in the first quarter, a pass that should have been a 59-yard touchdown connection, but the $3 million receiver dropped it. He later found Ryan Wingo for another perfect pass, a 50-yarder that put the Horns up 17-3. Manning celebrated with a swaggy strut similar to what WWE fans get from the hulking Oba Femi. He later found Ryan Wingo for another perfect pass, a 50-yarder that put the Horns up 17-3. Manning celebrated with a swaggy strut similar to what WWE fans get from the hulking Oba Femi. Remember, this is the same player who entered the season with a streak of having thrown 119 consecutive passes without an interception. In 2025, he averaged only one interception for every 58 passes. A Mississippi Rebels defender bats down a pass from Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) in the first quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. He's completed 63.3% of his passes, a number that needs to be five points higher if the Horns are to reach the postseason. Mississippi State has fallen on some tough times with three straight losses, the most recent coming against Oklahoma where star quarterback Kamario Taylor left in the first half after sustaining a lower body injury, but the Horns can't assume anything. They must return to playing to a higher standard on offense and it starts with the most visible guy. Edge or no edge, he has to be more consistent. Roast beef beats Ramen all day long. item.title: Badgers flip 4 star LB from Big Ten school after big win
item.description: PASADENA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Luke Fickell of the Wisconsin Badgers looks on against the UCLA Bruins during the first quarter at Rose Bowl Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Pasadena, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers secured a big win over the USC Trojans on Saturday night, improving to 5-2 on the season as they jumped into the AP Top 25 at No. 25. Not only did the Badgers secure the win on the field, but they also got a major win off the field. On Sunday, four-star linebacker Blake Betton announced that he flipped his commitment from Penn State to Wisconsin, giving the Badgers another blue-chip player in the 2027 class. Betton was in attendance for Wisconsin’s 24-7 win over USC on Saturday, and reports heading into the weekend suggested that it was more likely than not that the linebacker was making a flip in his recruitment. The Badgers had been early contenders in Betton’s recruitment, offering him back in September of 2025. However, Penn State gained traction after the hiring of Matt Campbell as head coach, and Betton committed to the Nittany Lions in April. Still, Wisconsin stayed the course and was able to get a key flip, acquiring their third linebacker in the 2027 class. Betton joins three-star Nathan Jones and three-star Keaton Wollan as the linebackers now in Wisconsin’s upcoming recruiting class. A Minnesota native, Betton had over two dozen offers in his recruitment and had been receiving interest from several Big Ten teams, including Michigan and Michigan State. He is ranked the third-best player in the state of Minnesota by Rivals and the fourth-best player in the state by ESPN and 247Sports.

item.title: Max Verstappen Absolutely Torches Red Bull After Grabbing 3rd in Austin: “Nothing Worked”
item.description: When you cross the finish line to secure a hard-fought podium at the United States Grand Prix, the team radio is usually filled with cheers and congratulations. However, if your name is Max Verstappen and your car handled like a shopping cart with a broken wheel for 56 laps, the post-race debrief is going to be incredibly spicy. Even though Verstappen managed to drag his RB22 to a third-place finish behind race-winner Kimi Antonelli and Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc , the Dutchman was absolutely furious with Red Bull’s execution on Sunday. The frustration had been brewing all afternoon. After spending a chunk of the race screaming about being stuck in the dirty air of his teammate Isack Hadjar and dealing with an “undriveable” braking issue, Verstappen let the pit wall have it the second the checkered flag waved. “Yeah, that was terrible,” Verstappen vented over the team radio. “The pace, the wrong tyre, shit pitstop, shit engine braking. Nothing worked. Lucky with the VSC at the end.” The late Virtual Safety Car he referenced is entirely the reason he kept his trophy. Had the race stayed green, a charging Lewis Hamilton would have likely blown past the struggling Red Bull in the closing laps. Verstappen: “Probably Not the Right Ones” Once the helmet came off, Verstappen cooled down slightly but maintained his brutal honesty during his post-race interview with Martin Brundle. When asked about his lack of grip in the final stages, Max pointed directly at the team’s setup choices. “I think our overall pace was not good enough, and then probably also the tyres that we had available were probably not the right ones,” Verstappen explained. “So, that’s something that we have to understand, because the last few races it was always working well for us.” AUSTIN, TEXAS – OCTOBER 24: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610240856 // Usage for editorial use only // Instead of throwing a complete tantrum, he accepted the reality of his fortunate finish. “For whatever reason it didn’t work out here, but we still managed to get on the podium,” he noted. “Maybe a little bit lucky with the VSC at the end, but I’ll take it.” Survival Mode Against Norris The one major highlight of Verstappen’s afternoon was a ruthless, extraordinary overtake on Lando Norris. McLaren foolishly gambled by leaving Norris out on old hard tyres, turning him into a sitting duck for the front-runners. When Brundle praised the aggressive move, noting that Leclerc was right on Max’s gearbox at the time, Verstappen shrugged it off as pure racing survival. “I had to,” Verstappen stated bluntly. “It was either get overtaken, or you have to go for the overtake, so that’s what I did.”

item.title: Mbappe Gets 8, Bellingham With 7.5 | Real Madrid Players Rated In Narrow Win Vs Barcelona
item.description: Mbappe Gets 8, Bellingham With 7.5 | Real Madrid Players Rated In Narrow Win Vs Barcelona Real Madrid faced off against Barcelona at the Nou Camp earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a good result on the road in La Liga. Los Blancos made a bright start to the game and took the lead in the 41st minute thanks to Kylian Mbappe’s goal. Jose Mourinho’s men went into the half-time break 1-0 up on the scoreline. Raphinha equalised for the Catalan club in the 61st minute before Mbappe scored again for the Madrid giants in the 87th minute. The Clasico ended with Real Madrid securing a narrow 2-1 win at the Nou Camp. Let’s take a look at how each Real Madrid player fared during the clash against Barcelona. GK: Andriy Lunin – 7/10 He made his fair share of saves during the game and did well to limit the opposition to just one goal. RB: Federico Valverde – 6.5/10 Valverde performed his defensive responsibilities well but offered very little going forward. CB: Ibrahima Konate – 6.5/10 He was a rock at the back and did well to keep Raphinha frustrated for most of the game. CB: Dean Huijsen – 7/10 Huijsen made a lot of crucial clearances on the defensive end of the field. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) LB: Marc Cucurella – 7/10 He was solid when defending inside his half but struggled to catch the eye inside the Barcelona half. RW: Arda Guler – 7.5/10 Guler was a constant menace from the right flank but there was no goal for him. CM: Aurelien Tchouameni – 6.5/10 He anchored the midfield relatively well and made one good chance in the final third. CM: Bernardo Silva – 6/10 Silva worked hard defensively but lacked quality on the ball. LW: Jude Bellingham – 7.5/10 He came back to defend when he could and made a few decent runs with the ball. item.title: Iowa State volleyball falls in four
item.description: HOUSTON — Iowa State dropped a four-set Big 12 volleyball match to Houston on Sunday afternoon, falling by set scores of 25-21, 20-25, 25-17, 25-20. The loss brings Iowa State to 12-8 overall and 6-3 in Big 12 play, while Houston improved to 12-8 overall and 5-4 in conference action. Despite the setback, Iowa State’s Mesaiya Bettis logged a career-high and match-leading 23 kills while hitting .436. The performance marked the first 20-plus kill match of her career and her fourth consecutive contest finishing in double figures. Alea Goolsby was the second Cyclone with double-digit kills, recording 12 kills while hitting .345. Defensively, Rachel Van Gorp led Iowa State with 21 digs, marking her seventh match with 20 or more digs this season and the 20th of her career. Van Gorp also contributed six assists and three service aces, while Nayeli Ti’a added 14 digs. Iowa State opened the match with a 3-0 lead in the first set following kills from Bettis and Goolsby, but Houston rallied to claim the opening set 25-21. The Cyclones answered in the second set, using a late scoring spree featuring three Bettis kills to capture a 25-20 victory and tie the match. Houston controlled the tempo in the third set to earn a 25-17 victory. In the fourth set, Iowa State built an early 6-3 lead before Houston responded with five consecutive points. Although Iowa State saved four match points late in the frame, Houston closed out the set 25-20 to secure the match. Next up Iowa State returns home for a two-match homestand, hosting West Virginia on Friday at 6:30 p.m. before facing No. 17 Kansas on Sunday at noon.

item.description: Pistons' Ausar Thompson ruled out against Sixers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday night, the Detroit Pistons are set to take on the Philadelphia 76ers , in a match that will see one of the two unbeaten teams have their stellar records come to an end. In his place, the aforementioned Bickerstaff has the likes of Duncan Robinson and Isiah Joe, amongst others, to choose from. It'll be an interesting match for Joe if he is to receive additional playing time, given that he used to play in the City of Brotherly Love, making 96 appearances for the Sixers, the team that drafted him in the second round of the 2020 NBA Draft. Tip-off between Detroit and Philadelphia is slated for 7:00 p.m. EST. item.title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix, but maiden F1 title must wait
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes competes at the free practice three at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, ahead of the United States Formula One Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Antonelli wins US Grand Prix, but maiden F1 title must wait») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes won the Formula One United States Grand Prix on Sunday but must wait at least another race to clinch his maiden title. The race in Austin offered Antonelli a first chance to clinch the trophy and become F1's youngest ever driver at 20 years old, but the Italian needed an unlike combination of results. He at least did his part and after a spectacular start from pole position, giving Red Bull's Max Verstappen no chance, Antonelli benefitted from a one-stop strategy and cruised to victory. "It was a result we needed, the whole team deserve it so much. All this time, putting so much work in to bring the new package... It was perfect execution from strategy to make the one-stop (work)," the Mercedes driver said. Antonelli is now 123 points ahead of Russell, with 125 points left on the table. He will claim the title in Mexico next week if he finishes at least in ninth. "What a boy... He just delivered from the beginning to the end, it was exceptional," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said. "It would definitely be lots of tequila on ice (next weekend) but he still needs to finish the race." Four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel, now retired, is currently the youngest F1 champion. He won his first title at 23 years, 134 days in 2010. Charles Leclerc of Ferrari was second after overtaking Verstappen with six laps to go. The Dutchman had to settle for third following victories in the past two races in Malaysia and Singapore. "It was quite a good race, unfortunately we came short of the victory. But it was positive We had good pace, it was a fun race with good battles," Leclerc said. Verstappen, who wasn't happy with second place in Saturday's qualifying, said that Red Bull's pace "was not good enough, and the tyres we had available were not the right ones." "We still managed to get on the podium, maybe a bit lucky with the virtual safety car at the end," he said. The virtual safety car was deployed with four laps to go after Valtteri Bottas parked up his Cadillac next to a service road. It was good for Verstappen because it neutralized Lewis Hamilton's charge to the podium with his Ferrari. Hamilton was fourth followed by the McLaren of defending champion Lando Norris and the Red Bull of Isack Hadjar. Oscar Piastri was seventh in the second McLaren. Mercedes' George Russell was eighth after receiving a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining advantage. Antonelli needed to win the race and for Russell to be not better than ninth and Hamilton not better than fifth to win the title. Liam Lawson of Racing Bulls and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completed the top 10.

item.title: How Kimi Antonelli can clinch his maiden F1 championship in Mexico
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli will have another chance to claim his maiden Formula 1 championship at next weekend's Mexican Grand Prix after narrowly missing out on securing the title in Austin. The 20-year-old converted pole position into his ninth win of the season at the United States Grand Prix, but Lewis Hamilton's fourth place and George Russell's eighth kept the title fight alive for at least another week. What does Kimi Antonelli need to do to win the F1 title in Mexico? If Antonelli finishes in the top nine in Mexico City next Sunday, he will be champion. It would not matter what Russell and Hamilton do in that scenario. After Mexico, four races remain if all goes as planned in Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with a maximum of 100 points available. Antonelli needs to finish the Mexican Grand Prix at least 100 points clear of both rivals. Even if Russell won in Mexico and Antonelli finished ninth, he would only cut the gap to exactly 100, and he would then have to win all four remaining races while Antonelli failed to score. But even then, Antonelli would win the title on countback. He already has nine grand prix wins this season, while Russell has three and could only reach a maximum of eight. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou, and he led them out again with a late, late victory that opens up a whole new world. With three minutes remaining and the energy with which they had played dropping, a wonderful piece of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run on a night in which there were so many of them. Camavinga sprinted into the area, slipped away from Pau Cubarsí and pulled the ball back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and Madrid had won it, Mbappé getting his second goal of a special match to end Barcelona’s record nine-game winning run. So much for a battering, so much for Barcelona going nine points clear, the title race run before November; there is life in Madrid and in this league. item.content:encoded: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou, and he led them out again with a late, late victory that opens up a whole new world. With three minutes remaining and the energy with which they had played dropping, a wonderful piece of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run on a night in which there were so many of them. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and Madrid had won it, Mbappé getting his second goal of a special match to end Barcelona’s record nine-game winning run. item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
